newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. February consumer price index (CPI), dealers said on Wednesday.
The consumer price index for February is forecast to show an increase of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.1 percent gain reported in January.

"Rates were narrowly mixed in the morning on some position adjustments, amid uncertainty over the market direction. But some people are waiting for fresh clues from tonight's release of the consumer price index for February," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the day," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday and Thursday/Friday eased 1/16 percentage point each to a common 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent, respectively.
Week-fixed rose 1/8 point to 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, partly due to the upcoming end of the Japanese fiscal year.

Among longer dates, one-month rose 1/16 point 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, three-months rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, nine-months was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-15/16 5-13/16 percent and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 6-1/8 6 percent.
